newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, JAN 27-SUNDAY, FEB 2.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, JAN 27-SUNDAY, FEB 2.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
BRUSSELS - EU finance ministers meet (Monday); hold open debate on Dutch EU presidency working programme.

BRUSSELS - European Commission holds seminar on "East-west anti-dumping policy" (Monday-Tuesday); speakers include European Commissioners Brittan and van den Broek, Czech Trade and Industry Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, UNICE Secretary General Francois Perigot.
THE HAGUE - Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo meets Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer (Monday); discussions focus on EU-east Asian relations and East Timor.
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday); orientation debate on priorities for 1998 budget.
BRUSSELS - European Commissioners Brittan, Marin, Fischler and Bangemann meet Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer - followed by a news conference with Commissioner Brittan (Wednesday).
BRUSSELS - European Parliament holds mini session (Wednesday-Thursday); debates fight against racism and terrorism (Wednesday).

BRUSSELS - Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov attends EP Foreign Affairs Committee and meets EP President Jose Maria Gil Robles; meets NATO Secretary General Javier Solana (Wednesday); meets European Commission President Santer and Commissioner van den Broek followed by a news conference (Thursday).
BRUSSELS - European People's Party holds news conference on "Fighting together against terrorism in the EU" (Wednesday).
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee holds plenary session (Wednesday-Thursday); European Commissioner Cresson attends (Thursday).

THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency launches "Year against racism and xenophobia" (Thursday); EP President Jose Marie Gil Robles signs declaration with European Commission President Santer, European Commissioner Flynn and Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok.
BONN - German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Spanish Prime Minister Jose Aznar meet (Thursday); main discussions focus on reform of the EU and preparations for the Amsterdam EU summit.
AMSTERDAM - EU transport ministers hold informal council (Friday-Saturday); main discussions focus on EU-Swizterland transport relations.
THE HAGUE - EU Industry ministers hold informal council (Saturday-Sunday); main discussions focus on EU's global competitiveness, particularly in information and communication technology.
MONDAY, JANUARY 27
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - ECOFIN Council (1000/0900 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Presentation of the Dutch EU presidency programme/work programme of the Commission (open debate at 1000/0900 GMT).
- Commission names jury for competition to design new Euro coins.
- Commission information on financial assistance to third countries.
- New EIB lending mandates for Central and eastern European Countries/Baltic States, Mediterranean countries, Latin America and South Africa.
- (Before lunch) Structured dialogue with Central and Eastern European Countries - followed by lunch.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Inter-governmental conference (IGC) representatives meet (and Tuesday).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds seminar on "East-west anti-dumping policy" (and Tuesday). Main discussions focus on the way anti-dumping rules are applied and the views of business and government in Central and Eastern European Countries - news conference at 1140/1040 GMT. Speakers include: European Commissioners Brittan and van den Broek, Czech Trade and Industry Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, UNICE Secretary General Francois Perigot. Venue: Renaissance Hotel.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1500/1400 GMT) Foreign Affairs - holds public hearing -
European Commissioner van den Broek
attends;
Agriculture - European Commissioner
Fischler attends;
External Economic Relations;
Culture;
Civil Liberties;
Institutional Affairs;
Petitions.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Group of the European People's Party (EPP) holds conference on SMEs (1400/1300 GMT). Venue: EP, Leo 03C50. Contact: EPP, SMEs Association (322) 284 4717.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Consultation among churches and their organisations in the EU on issues of poverty and social exclusion holds it's final meeting (1500/1400 GMT). Venue: EP, Belliard 51. Contact: Hans Joergen Torkelund (322) 230 5792.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "A free trade agreement with Russia?" (1315/1215 GMT). Speaker is Russian Mission to the EU Deputy Head Ivan Ivanov. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
THE HAGUE - Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo meets Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer; discussions focus on EU-east Asian relations and East Timor - followed by a news conference.
TUESDAY, JANUARY 28
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer attends Council of Europe.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Agriculture;
Foreign Affairs;
External Economic Relations;
Culture;
Civil Liberties;
Institutional Affairs;
Petitions;
Inquiry Committee on Transit - European
Commissioner Monti attends;
- (1500/1400 GMT) Culture;
Institutional Affairs;
Committee of Inquiry into BSE.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "The passage to the euro" (1230/1130 GMT). Speakers include: former Bundesbank President Schlesinger. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 29

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioners Brittan, Marin, Fischler and Bangemann meet Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer - followed by a news conference with Commissioner Brittan at 1440/1340 GMT. Downer addresses press breakfast on "Australia, Asia and Europe" (0800/0700 GMT) at the Conrad Hotel.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0800 GMT).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner Liikanen on priorities for 1998 budget - orientation debate.
- Commissioner Fischler communication on olives and olive oil.
- Commissioner Monti communication on the proposal for directive on the application of VAT to telecoms.
- Commissioner Bjerregaard communication on environmental responsabilities - orientation debate.
- European Commissioners Bjerregaard and Monti communication on environmental taxes and levies in the internal market.
- European Commission President Santer and Commissioners Wulf-Mathies and Flynn communcation on objective 2 programming for agriculture and document on objective 2 programming in Germany.
BRUSSELS - European Parliament holds mini session (and Thursday).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (1500/1400 GMT) Commission communication on topical and urgent subjects of major importance.
- (1600/1500 GMT) Annual debate on the fight against racism.
- Viviane Reding report on the fight against terrorism in the EU.
- Jose Luis Valverde Lopez report on the EU's progress in 1995 in applying article D of the EU treaty.
- Jose Antonio Escudero report on the European Commission's first report on taking account of the cultural aspects in EU action, COM(96)160.

- (possibly) Barbara Schmidbauer report on the Commission's green paper on "Towards an equal and efficient tariff in transport - option in the internalisation of external transport costs in the EU", COM(95)691.
- Alessandro Danesin report on "Towards a new maritime strategy", COM(96)81.
- Pedro Marset Campos report on Community research and sustainable development policy.
- Juan de Dios Izquierdo Collado report on a multiannual programme establishing Community statistics in research, development and innovation, COM(96)42.
- Anne Marie Schaffner report on the Commission's thirteenth annual report on the control of the application of Community law, COM(96)600.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov attends EP Foreign Affairs Committee at 1100/1000 GMT; meets EP President Jose Maria Gil Robles at 1230/1130 - followed by lunch; meets NATO Secretary General Javier Solana at 1425/1325 GMT.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committee meets:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Civil Liberties - European Commissioner
Flynn attends.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Group of the European People's Party (PPE) holds news conference on "Fighting together against terrorism in the EU" (1400/1300 GMT). Venue: EP press room. Contact: Katrin Ruhrmann, EPP (322) 284 2573.
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (1430/1330 GMT) (and Thursday).
Agenda includes:
- European advisory committee on statistical information in the economic and social spheres, COM(96)439.
- Action programme for integrated groundwater protection and management, COM(96)315.
- Monitoring mechanism of Community CO2 and other greenhouse gas emissions, COM(96)369.
- Review of the Community strategy for waste management, COM(96)399.
- Maximum residue limits of veterinary medicinal products on foodstuffs of animal origin, COM(96)584.
- Amendment of regulation on the Community trade mark to give effect to EC accession to the protocol relating to the Madrid agreement, COM(96)372.
- EC accession to the protocol relating to the Madrid agreement concerning the international registration of marks, COM(96)367.
- Standardisation and the global information society, COM(96)359.
- Community strategy to reduce CO2 emissions from passenger cars, COM(95)689.
- Approximation of laws relating to fertilizers, COM(96)594.
- Action to promote combined goods transport, COM(96)335.
- Amendment of social security schemes - migrant workers, COM(96)452.
- Development of the social dialogue at European level, COM(96)448.
- Stocktaking of the first three years of CAP reform.
- Community fisheries and aquaculture system, COM(96)350.
- Relations between the EU and the countries bordering the Baltic Sea.
- EU/ASEAN relations.
THURSDAY, JANUARY 30

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner van den Broek meet Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov; Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov holds news conference at 1800/1700 GMT at the Bulgarian EU Mission, 7 ave Moscicki. Contact: Bulgarian EU Mission (322) 374 5860.
BRUSSELS - European Parliament holds mini session (second of two days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (0900/0800 GMT) (possibly) Anne Van Lancker report on Schengen: evaluation, insertion in Community law, cooperation with third countries.
- Irini Lambraki report on the application of article K9.
- (1100/1000 GMT) Votes on:
- Proposal for resolution on the annual debate on the fight against racism;
- Reports on the application of cooperation procedures, codecision and request for assent;
- Proposals for resolution on the outcome of the December 19-20 Fisheries Council;
- Other proposals for resolution in closed debate.
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (1000/0900 GMT) (second of two days). European Commissioner Cresson attends at 1000/0900 GMT.

BRUSSELS - European Insurance Committee holds news conference on "European insurance this year" (1130/1030 GMT). Venue: European Insurance Committee, 29 square de Meeus. Contact: European Insurance Committee (322) 547 5811.

DIEGEM, Belgium - De Financieel Economische Tijd holds conference on "European lie: what are the risks of EMU?" (0900/0800 GMT). Venue: Sofitel Hotel, Bessenveldstraat 15. Contact: Tijd Academie (323) 286 0460.

THE HAGUE (EXPANDED ITEM) - Dutch EU presidency launches "Year against racism and xenophobia". EP President Jose Marie Gil Robles gives address at 1520/1420 GMT; signs declaration with European Commission President Santer, European Commissioner Flynn and Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok at 1620/1520 GMT.
BONN - German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Spanish Prime Minister Jose Aznar meet; main discussions focus on the reform of the EU and preparations for the Amsterdam EU summit.
FRIDAY, JANUARY 31

AMSTERDAM - Informal Transport Council (1400/1300 GMT) (and Saturday). Discussions focus on EU/Switzerland air and land transport relations, talks which are linked to the EU's internal discussions on road pricing and the European Commission's proposal for a revised "Eurovignette" system COM(96)331 and the inter-operability of road-pricing systems.
DAVOS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer, Commissioners Brittan, Marin and de Silguy attend the world economic forum (and Saturday).
SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 1

AMSTERDAM (NEW ITEM) - Informal Transport Council (0930/0830 GMT) (second of two days). Discussions focus on Commission proposal on a negotiating mandate setting up a European civil aviation safety body and on its air traffic management white paper COM(96)57.
THE HAGUE - Informal Industry Council (and Sunday). Main discussions focus on EU's global competitiveness, particularly in information and communication technology.
SUNDAY, FEBRUARY 2
No events scheduled.
